question.text: What do solid white fog lines mark, and may you cross them to pass?

answer.text: Solid white fog lines mark the right edge of the road and help you stay on it at night or in bad weather, and crossing them to pass is illegal.

teaching.text: The fog line keeps you on the road in the dark, and it is never a passing lane. Remember: fog line, never pass over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Solid white fog lines mark the right edge of the road and help you stay on it at night or in bad weather, and crossing them to pass is illegal.

question.text: Where do solid white lines separate lanes, and should you cross them?

answer.text: Solid white lines also separate same-direction lanes where lane changes are risky, such as sharp curves and freeway acceleration and deceleration lanes, and you should not cross them.

teaching.text: Solid white between lanes marks places where changing lanes is risky. Remember: solid white: stay put.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Solid white lines also separate same-direction lanes where lane changes are risky, such as sharp curves and freeway acceleration and deceleration lanes, and you should not cross them.

question.text: What does a double solid white line separate, and may you cross it?

answer.text: A double solid white line separates two same-direction travel paths, and crossing it is prohibited.

teaching.text: Two solid white lines mean the paths beside each other must stay apart. Remember: double white, never cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A double solid white line separates two same-direction travel paths, and crossing it is prohibited.

question.text: How are crosswalks marked?

answer.text: Crosswalks are marked by solid white lines painted across the pavement or by white stripes laid in the direction of traffic, at intersections and sometimes midblock.

teaching.text: Crosswalks can be lines across the road or stripes running with traffic. Remember: white lines mark crosswalks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crosswalks are marked by solid white lines painted across the pavement or by white stripes laid in the direction of traffic, at intersections and sometimes midblock.

question.text: Where do you stop at a crosswalk?

answer.text: Stop behind the crosswalk line.

teaching.text: Stopping behind the crosswalk keeps people from walking around your car into traffic. Remember: stop behind the crosswalk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop behind the crosswalk line.

question.text: What does a stop line show?

answer.text: A stop line is a wide white line across a lane showing where to stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic.

teaching.text: The wide white line is where your front bumper stops. Remember: wide white line, stop here.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stop line is a wide white line across a lane showing where to stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic.

question.text: Where do you stop when there is no stop line or crosswalk?

answer.text: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection, and in every case make sure you can see traffic from all directions before going.

teaching.text: No line means stop before the intersection, then make sure you can see. Remember: stop before the intersection.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection, and in every case make sure you can see traffic from all directions before going.

question.text: What do wide white arrows in a lane show?

answer.text: Wide white arrows down the middle of a lane show the movements allowed from it; in the handbook example the far-right lane is right turn only, the next lane allows right or straight, and turning right from the other two lanes is illegal.

teaching.text: The arrows in your lane are rules for which way you may go. Remember: arrows show allowed moves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wide white arrows down the middle of a lane show the movements allowed from it; in the handbook example the far-right lane is right turn only, the next lane allows right or straight, and turning right from the other two lanes is illegal.

question.text: Who may use a bicycle lane?

answer.text: A bicycle lane, shown by special markings and signs, is reserved only for bicyclists.

teaching.text: The lane belongs to bicyclists alone. Remember: bike lanes are for bikes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A bicycle lane, shown by special markings and signs, is reserved only for bicyclists.

question.text: What does green paint in a bike lane flag?

answer.text: Green paint in a bike lane flags a likely conflict point between cars and bicycles, usually at intersections and driveways, so take extra care turning there.

teaching.text: Green patches mark the places where turning cars and bikes meet. Remember: green paint, conflict point.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Green paint in a bike lane flags a likely conflict point between cars and bicycles, usually at intersections and driveways, so take extra care turning there.

question.text: Which actions are illegal in a bike lane?

answer.text: Driving, passing, turning right, parking, pulling over to wait, or making a delivery in a bike lane is illegal.

teaching.text: Even a quick stop in a bike lane forces riders into traffic. Remember: no driving, parking, waiting.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving, passing, turning right, parking, pulling over to wait, or making a delivery in a bike lane is illegal.

question.text: What do shared lane markings tell you?

answer.text: Shared lane markings show proper lane position and traffic flow, and when you see one, watch for bicyclists and give them room as legal road users.

teaching.text: Bicyclists are legal road users in a shared lane, so give them room. Remember: share the lane with bikes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Shared lane markings show proper lane position and traffic flow, and when you see one, watch for bicyclists and give them room as legal road users.

question.text: What do yellow lines separate, and what types are there?

answer.text: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and come as solid, broken and center-lane lines.

teaching.text: Yellow on your left means traffic beyond it comes toward you. Remember: yellow means opposite directions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and come as solid, broken and center-lane lines.

question.text: What does a single broken yellow center line usually allow?

answer.text: A single broken yellow center line on a two-way road usually means you may pass when it is safe.

teaching.text: A broken yellow line is permission to consider passing, only when safe. Remember: broken yellow, pass safely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single broken yellow center line on a two-way road usually means you may pass when it is safe.

question.text: May you cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass?

answer.text: Do not cross a solid yellow line on your side of the center line to pass.

teaching.text: Read the line closest to you; solid on your side means no passing. Remember: solid on your side, stay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not cross a solid yellow line on your side of the center line to pass.

question.text: Where does a solid yellow line mark the left edge?

answer.text: On a four-lane divided road or a one-way road, a solid yellow line usually marks the pavement's left edge.

teaching.text: On divided and one-way roads, yellow marks your left edge. Remember: yellow left edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a four-lane divided road or a one-way road, a solid yellow line usually marks the pavement's left edge.

question.text: What does a double solid yellow center line ban, and when may you cross it?

answer.text: A double solid yellow center line on a two-lane road bans passing in both directions, though you may cross it to turn into a driveway or crossroad or reach a parking spot.

teaching.text: Crossing a double yellow to turn is fine; crossing it to pass is not. Remember: double yellow, no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A double solid yellow center line on a two-lane road bans passing in both directions, though you may cross it to turn into a driveway or crossroad or reach a parking spot.

question.text: How is a left-turn-only center lane marked, and who may use it?

answer.text: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines inside, and left turns may be made from it in either direction.

teaching.text: Drivers from both directions share the center lane to turn left. Remember: center lane, lefts both ways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines inside, and left turns may be made from it in either direction.

question.text: May you use the center turn lane to pass or merge?

answer.text: Using the left-turn-only center lane to pass or merge is illegal and dangerous.

teaching.text: Speeding along the center lane can meet a turning driver head on. Remember: center lane is for turning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Using the left-turn-only center lane to pass or merge is illegal and dangerous.

question.text: How do the lines of a center turn lane read, and what is it never for?

answer.text: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines on its inner edges, and it serves left turns from either direction but never passing or merging.

teaching.text: Solid lines outside, broken inside, and never a passing lane. Remember: solid outside, broken inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines on its inner edges, and it serves left turns from either direction but never passing or merging.

question.text: How do broken, solid and double solid yellow lines differ for passing?

answer.text: A broken yellow center line allows passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids it, and a double solid yellow forbids it for both directions.

teaching.text: Broken allows passing when safe; solid on your side and double solid forbid it. Remember: broken yes, solid no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A broken yellow center line allows passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids it, and a double solid yellow forbids it for both directions.

question.text: What does every type of yellow line have in common?

answer.text: Any yellow line, whether solid, broken or a center-lane line, separates traffic moving in opposite directions.

teaching.text: Any yellow pattern means the far side moves the other way. Remember: yellow splits opposite traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any yellow line, whether solid, broken or a center-lane line, separates traffic moving in opposite directions.

question.text: What is a Michigan Left?

answer.text: Michigan Lefts, or indirect left turns, have been used since the late 1960s; where they exist you cannot turn left directly but drive straight or turn right and then U-turn at a median crossover.

teaching.text: Where a Michigan Left exists, a direct left is not allowed. Remember: straight or right, then U-turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Michigan Lefts, or indirect left turns, have been used since the late 1960s; where they exist you cannot turn left directly but drive straight or turn right and then U-turn at a median crossover.

question.text: How many vehicles fit a single-lane crossover, and why is it wide?

answer.text: A single-lane Michigan Left crossover takes one vehicle at a time; extra width is there for tractor trailers and RVs that need a wider turn.

teaching.text: Wide crossovers leave room for big rigs, not for a second car. Remember: one at a time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single-lane Michigan Left crossover takes one vehicle at a time; extra width is there for tractor trailers and RVs that need a wider turn.

question.text: When may two vehicles turn together at a crossover?

answer.text: A multi-lane Michigan Left lets two vehicles turn together when arrows, ONLY lettering and solid white lines show it, and an unmarked crossover is always treated as single-lane.

teaching.text: Arrows, ONLY lettering and white lines are what make two lanes. Remember: two only when marked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A multi-lane Michigan Left lets two vehicles turn together when arrows, ONLY lettering and solid white lines show it, and an unmarked crossover is always treated as single-lane.

question.text: How do you make a Michigan Left from the main highway?

answer.text: From the main highway, drive past the intersection, turn left into the median crossover, then turn left back onto the main highway when clear, and then either keep going straight or get into the far-right lane to make a right onto the cross road.

teaching.text: From the main highway: drive past, U-turn at the crossover, then go straight or right. Remember: past, crossover, back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From the main highway, drive past the intersection, turn left into the median crossover, then turn left back onto the main highway when clear, and then either keep going straight or get into the far-right lane to make a right onto the cross road.

question.text: How do you make a Michigan Left from the cross road?

answer.text: From the cross road, turn right onto the main highway, move to the far-left lane, turn left into the median crossover, and when clear turn left onto the main highway and continue straight.

teaching.text: From the cross road: right turn first, then far left, then the crossover. Remember: right, far left, crossover.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From the cross road, turn right onto the main highway, move to the far-left lane, turn left into the median crossover, and when clear turn left onto the main highway and continue straight.

question.text: How do you treat an unmarked Michigan Left crossover?

answer.text: A Michigan Left crossover with no markings is always single-lane, even if it looks wide enough for two cars, because that width is for large vehicles.

teaching.text: No markings means one vehicle at a time. Remember: unmarked means single-lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Michigan Left crossover with no markings is always single-lane, even if it looks wide enough for two cars, because that width is for large vehicles.

question.text: Where do yield lines appear, and where do you stop?

answer.text: Yield lines appear at roundabouts and midblock crosswalks, and when yielding you stop behind them.

teaching.text: When you must yield, your stopping place is behind the yield line. Remember: stop behind yield lines.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield lines appear at roundabouts and midblock crosswalks, and when yielding you stop behind them.

question.text: What do white triangles across a lane mean?

answer.text: White triangles painted across a lane mean be ready to stop and yield to pedestrians.

teaching.text: Painted triangles act like yield signs on the pavement. Remember: triangles mean yield to walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White triangles painted across a lane mean be ready to stop and yield to pedestrians.

question.text: What do dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark?

answer.text: Dashed white lines across a lane in a roundabout mark the edge of its circular lane.

teaching.text: The dashes show where the circle's lane begins. Remember: dashes mark the circle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Dashed white lines across a lane in a roundabout mark the edge of its circular lane.

question.text: May you cut through a parking lot to avoid a traffic signal?

answer.text: Driving through a store parking lot or any other public or private property to get around a traffic-control device is illegal.

teaching.text: Cutting through a lot to skip a signal is illegal on any property. Remember: no shortcuts around signals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving through a store parking lot or any other public or private property to get around a traffic-control device is illegal.

question.text: How do white triangles differ from dashed white lines in a roundabout?

answer.text: White triangles across a lane are pedestrian yield lines, while dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark the edge of the circle.

teaching.text: Triangles are about people; dashes are about the circle. Remember: triangles yield, dashes edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White triangles across a lane are pedestrian yield lines, while dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark the edge of the circle.

question.text: What does a red light mean?

answer.text: A red light, at the top of Michigan signals, means stop behind the crosswalk or stop line.

teaching.text: Stop behind the crosswalk or stop line at every red. Remember: red: stop behind the line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A red light, at the top of Michigan signals, means stop behind the crosswalk or stop line.

question.text: What does a yellow light require?

answer.text: A yellow light means the signal is about to turn red, and you are required to stop; when a safe stop is impossible, do not accelerate, and go through the intersection with caution.

teaching.text: Yellow is a signal to stop when you safely can, never to speed up. Remember: yellow means stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A yellow light means the signal is about to turn red, and you are required to stop; when a safe stop is impossible, do not accelerate, and go through the intersection with caution.

question.text: What does a green light mean?

answer.text: A green light means proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles.

teaching.text: Green means look again, then go with care. Remember: green: go with caution.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green light means proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles.

question.text: What do you do at a signal that is not working?

answer.text: If a signal is not working and no officer or other device controls traffic, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the right on a tie.

teaching.text: A dark signal works like an all-way stop. Remember: dark signal, all-way stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a signal is not working and no officer or other device controls traffic, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the right on a tie.

question.text: What must you do at a red light before moving on?

answer.text: At a red light, stop completely and check cross traffic and pedestrians before moving on green or turning right on red.

teaching.text: Stop completely, then check cross traffic and pedestrians before moving. Remember: stop, then check everyone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a red light, stop completely and check cross traffic and pedestrians before moving on green or turning right on red.

question.text: What does a flashing red light mean?

answer.text: A flashing red light means come to a full stop and go only when the road is clear.

teaching.text: Treat a flashing red like a stop sign. Remember: flashing red is a stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing red light means come to a full stop and go only when the road is clear.

question.text: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

answer.text: A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection carefully, scanning cross traffic both ways.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow asks for care, not a stop. Remember: flashing yellow, go carefully.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection carefully, scanning cross traffic both ways.

question.text: How does a steady yellow differ from a flashing yellow light?

answer.text: A steady yellow on a doghouse signal means stop if you have not entered the intersection, whereas a flashing yellow light lets you continue carefully through it.

teaching.text: Steady yellow stops you; flashing yellow lets you continue carefully. Remember: steady stops, flashing continues.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow on a doghouse signal means stop if you have not entered the intersection, whereas a flashing yellow light lets you continue carefully through it.

question.text: What does a doghouse signal control?

answer.text: The five-section-head or doghouse signal controls turns with red, yellow and green lights plus a yellow and a green turn arrow.

teaching.text: The doghouse adds a yellow and a green turn arrow to the usual lights. Remember: five lights for turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The five-section-head or doghouse signal controls turns with red, yellow and green lights plus a yellow and a green turn arrow.

question.text: How does a green arrow differ from a green light on a doghouse signal?

answer.text: A lit green arrow on a doghouse signal gives a protected turn with conflicting traffic stopped, while the green light lets you turn only after oncoming traffic clears.

teaching.text: An arrow means others are stopped; a ball means wait for a gap. Remember: arrow protects, light permits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lit green arrow on a doghouse signal gives a protected turn with conflicting traffic stopped, while the green light lets you turn only after oncoming traffic clears.

question.text: What does a yellow light or yellow arrow mean on a doghouse signal?

answer.text: On a doghouse signal, a yellow light or yellow arrow means red is coming, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely; if already in, finish the turn with care once traffic is clear.

teaching.text: Yellow says the turn time is ending, so stop unless you are already in. Remember: yellow arrow: red is coming.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a doghouse signal, a yellow light or yellow arrow means red is coming, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely; if already in, finish the turn with care once traffic is clear.

question.text: What does a steady green arrow mean?

answer.text: A steady green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may go the arrow's way with caution, still yielding to pedestrians in the intersection.

teaching.text: Even with a green arrow, pedestrians in the intersection come first. Remember: green arrow, oncoming stopped.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may go the arrow's way with caution, still yielding to pedestrians in the intersection.

question.text: How is the flashing yellow arrow signal built, and why?

answer.text: The flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal uses four separate lenses, a design federal highway research found moves traffic more efficiently and cuts crash chances.

teaching.text: Four lenses, better traffic flow and fewer crash chances. Remember: four lenses, fewer crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal uses four separate lenses, a design federal highway research found moves traffic more efficiently and cuts crash chances.

question.text: What does a solid red arrow mean?

answer.text: A solid red arrow means stop and do not turn until the signal changes.

teaching.text: No turning at all until the red arrow changes. Remember: red arrow, no turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid red arrow means stop and do not turn until the signal changes.

question.text: What does a solid yellow arrow warn?

answer.text: A solid yellow arrow warns the left-turn signal is about to turn red; stop if approaching, but if already in the intersection with no conflicting traffic you may finish the turn.

teaching.text: A solid yellow arrow means red is next, so stop if you are approaching. Remember: yellow arrow, red next.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid yellow arrow warns the left-turn signal is about to turn red; stop if approaching, but if already in the intersection with no conflicting traffic you may finish the turn.

question.text: When may you turn on a flashing yellow arrow?

answer.text: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic, which has a green light, and after checking for a safe gap and for crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.

teaching.text: Oncoming traffic has the green, so wait for a safe gap. Remember: flashing arrow: yield first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic, which has a green light, and after checking for a safe gap and for crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.

question.text: What does a solid green arrow mean on the flashing yellow arrow signal?

answer.text: A solid green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may turn left, still yielding to people in the crosswalk; with detection cameras or sensors this phase may be skipped when no one is waiting to turn.

teaching.text: A solid green arrow is the protected turn, and sensors may skip it. Remember: solid green arrow, protected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may turn left, still yielding to people in the crosswalk; with detection cameras or sensors this phase may be skipped when no one is waiting to turn.

question.text: What do pedestrian signals do, and what do some show?

answer.text: Pedestrian signals control crossing points, and some show audible or visual countdowns of the time left.

teaching.text: A countdown shows walkers how much crossing time is left. Remember: countdowns show time left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pedestrian signals control crossing points, and some show audible or visual countdowns of the time left.

question.text: What does WALK mean, and what about when it flashes?

answer.text: A walking person symbol or WALK means traffic must yield and pedestrians may cross; when it starts flashing, those already crossing should finish.

teaching.text: A flashing WALK means finish crossing, not start. Remember: walk means cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A walking person symbol or WALK means traffic must yield and pedestrians may cross; when it starts flashing, those already crossing should finish.

question.text: What does DONT WALK or a raised hand mean?

answer.text: DONT WALK or a red raised hand means do not cross, and drivers must always yield to pedestrians.

teaching.text: Whatever the walker's signal shows, drivers still yield. Remember: raised hand, do not cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: DONT WALK or a red raised hand means do not cross, and drivers must always yield to pedestrians.

question.text: What is a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon?

answer.text: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon is a crossing device that warns drivers of pedestrians, and its signal sequence has six steps.

teaching.text: The beacon's job is to warn you that people are crossing. Remember: beacon warns of walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon is a crossing device that warns drivers of pedestrians, and its signal sequence has six steps.

hooks_spoken: Fog lines and solid white lines are not for crossing; double solid white is prohibited.
Stop behind the stop line or crosswalk, or before the intersection if neither exists.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of white lines and stop lines. Fog lines and solid white lines are not for crossing; double solid white is prohibited. Stop behind the stop line or crosswalk, or before the intersection if neither exists. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Lane arrows show the moves allowed from each lane.
Bike lanes are for bikes only; green paint flags conflict points.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of lane arrows and bike lanes. Lane arrows show the moves allowed from each lane. Bike lanes are for bikes only; green paint flags conflict points. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Broken yellow allows passing when safe; solid on your side or double solid forbids it.
The center turn lane serves lefts both ways, never passing or merging.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yellow lines. Broken yellow allows passing when safe; solid on your side or double solid forbids it. The center turn lane serves lefts both ways, never passing or merging. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A Michigan Left means go straight or right, then U-turn at the crossover.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of michigan Lefts. A Michigan Left means go straight or right, then U-turn at the crossover. Unmarked crossovers are single-lane. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Stop behind yield lines; triangles mean yield to pedestrians.
Never cut through a lot to get around a signal.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yield markings and shortcuts. Stop behind yield lines; triangles mean yield to pedestrians. Never cut through a lot to get around a signal. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Red stops, yellow means stop if you safely can, green goes with caution.
Flashing red is a stop, flashing yellow is go carefully, and a dark signal is an all-way stop.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of traffic lights. Red stops, yellow means stop if you safely can, green goes with caution. Flashing red is a stop, flashing yellow is go carefully, and a dark signal is an all-way stop. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A green arrow protects your turn; a green light means yield first.
A flashing yellow arrow means yield to oncoming traffic before turning.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of turn arrows. A green arrow protects your turn; a green light means yield first. A flashing yellow arrow means yield to oncoming traffic before turning. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: WALK means cross, the raised hand means do not, and drivers always yield to pedestrians.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of pedestrian signals. WALK means cross, the raised hand means do not, and drivers always yield to pedestrians. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
